schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digits (d TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, login VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projects (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', description TEXT, homepage VARCHAR(255) DEFAULT '', is_public TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, status INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, parent_id INT DEFAULT NULL, created_on DATETIME DEFAULT NULL)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS enabled_modules (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, project_id INT DEFAULT NULL, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, KEY enabled_modules_project_id (project_id), KEY enabled_modules_name_project_id (name, project_id))

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS members (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, project_id INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_on DATETIME DEFAULT NULL, mail_notification TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, KEY index_members_on_user_id (user_id), KEY members_project_id (project_id))

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS issues (id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, tracker_id INT NOT NULL, project_id INT NOT NULL, subject VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', description LONGTEXT, due_date DATE DEFAULT NULL, category_id INT DEFAULT NULL, is_private TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, author_id INT NOT NULL, assigned_to_id INT DEFAULT NULL, KEY issues_project_id (project_id), KEY issues_author_id (author_id), KEY issues_assigned_to_id (assigned_to_id))
generation_sql: INSERT IGNORE INTO users (id, login) SELECT n, CONCAT('user_', n) FROM (SELECT d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1000*d4.d + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 CROSS JOIN digits d4 WHERE d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1000*d4.d + 1 <= 1350) seq

INSERT IGNORE INTO projects (id, name, description, homepage, is_public, status, parent_id, created_on) SELECT n, CONCAT('project_', n), '', '', 1, 1, NULL, '2020-01-01 00:00:00' FROM (SELECT d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 WHERE d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1 <= 494) seq
INSERT IGNORE INTO enabled_modules (id, project_id, name) SELECT id, id, 'issue_tracking' FROM projects

INSERT IGNORE INTO members (id, user_id, project_id, created_on, mail_notification) SELECT n, CASE WHEN n <= 20 THEN 44 ELSE 638 END, n, '2020-01-01 00:00:00', 0 FROM (SELECT d1.d + 10*d2.d + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 WHERE d1.d + 10*d2.d + 1 <= 40) seq

INSERT IGNORE INTO issues (id, tracker_id, project_id, subject, description, due_date, category_id, is_private, author_id, assigned_to_id) SELECT n, 1 + MOD(n, 5), CASE WHEN MOD(n, 30000) = 0 THEN 41 + MOD(n, 454) ELSE 1 + MOD(n - 1, 494) END, CASE WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 300) = 0 THEN CONCAT('old ticket ', n, ' 255392 hit') WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 17) = 0 THEN CONCAT('old ticket ', n, ' token 255392 near-miss') ELSE CONCAT('ticket ', n, ' filler') END, '', NULL, NULL, 0, CASE WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 8) = 0 THEN 44 ELSE 1 + MOD(n, 1350) END, CASE WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 12) = 0 THEN 44 WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 18) = 0 THEN 186 WHEN n <= 6000 AND MOD(n, 25) = 0 THEN 898 ELSE NULL END FROM (SELECT d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1000*d4.d + 10000*d5.d + 100000*d6.d + 1 AS n FROM digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 CROSS JOIN digits d3 CROSS JOIN digits d4 CROSS JOIN digits d5 CROSS JOIN digits d6 WHERE d1.d + 10*d2.d + 100*d3.d + 1000*d4.d + 10000*d5.d + 100000*d6.d + 1 <= 334823) seq
ANALYZE TABLE users, projects, enabled_modules, members, issues

tables.name: digits
tables.purpose: helper table to generate bounded row counts without external tooling

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: small dimension table matching the reported user count

tables.name: projects
tables.purpose: project dimension table used by the join and permission predicates
tables.distribution_notes: Mostly public projects with status 1; enough rows to cover the literal project-id lists in the query.

tables.name: enabled_modules
tables.purpose: one-row-per-project module table to satisfy the EXISTS predicate
tables.distribution_notes: Every project gets an issue_tracking row so the EXISTS check stays visible but not selective.

tables.name: members
tables.purpose: membership table used by the NOT IN subquery
tables.distribution_notes: Only projects 1-40 are associated with users 44 and 638, producing a small but non-empty exclusion set.

tables.name: issues
tables.purpose: large fact table whose cardinality and subject distribution drive the query cost
tables.distribution_notes: Model three key constraints explicitly: token match rate is very low overall, token hits are concentrated in low-id/old rows, and permission-passing rows are skewed so the effective hit rate among descending-primary-key candidates is tiny. Most rows are filler text; the 255392 token appears mainly in early ids and rarely in the high-id tail, forcing the ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10 scan to inspect many rows before it can stop.

value_skew.issues.subject: rare rows embed '255392'; most rows use filler text; token hits are intentionally concentrated in low-id rows and nearly absent in the high-id tail
value_skew.issues.assigned_to_id: skewed toward 44, 186, and 898 in older rows to preserve permission-branch visibility
value_skew.projects.is_public: all rows are public to keep the permission logic broad
value_skew.projects.status: all rows are non-9 to keep the status filter visible without eliminating the table

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(optimizer_switch='semijoin=off,materialization=off,in_to_exists=on') */ issues.* FROM issues FORCE INDEX (PRIMARY) STRAIGHT_JOIN projects ON projects.id = issues.project_id WHERE ((projects.status <> 9 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 AS one FROM enabled_modules em WHERE em.project_id = projects.id AND em.name = 'issue_tracking')) AND (((projects.is_public = 1 AND projects.id NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM members WHERE user_id IN (44, 638)) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (1, 6, 9, 13, 115, 129, 131, 136, 186, 227, 228, 230, 275, 287, 315, 335, 340, 369, 394, 404, 408, 450, 453, 454, 456, 458, 460, 462, 492, 511, 512, 516, 519, 527, 531, 533, 537) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (40, 68, 130, 149, 326, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 402, 455, 514, 515, 528) AND (1 = 1)) OR (projects.id IN (91, 111, 128, 130, 149, 235, 257, 322, 326, 328, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 489, 508, 514, 515, 525, 528) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (457) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))))) AND (issues.id != 251880) AND (LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%'))) ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10
calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the prepared data keeps the query issues-driven and that the descending primary-key path still has to search through many rows before finding enough token matches.
expected_evidence: The plan starts from issues using FORCE INDEX(PRIMARY) / primary-key access rather than a selective subject lookup.
The project, enabled_modules, and members checks remain visible as separate steps or subplans.
The subject filter remains a post-filter rather than becoming an indexed probe.
